title: Cluster 03 DRILL: Variation, Environment and the Chi-Squared Test
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 6 · 11 questions · 76 marks · 30 parts · roughly an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as for duplicated labels. Q1 the official chi-squared, end to end · Q2 degrees of freedom at six classes and at two · Q3 chi-squared on an epistatic ratio, where the merge fixes c · Q4 both branches of the conclusion, and which test to reach for · Q5 the MCQ that fuses the verdict with the linkage diagnosis · Q6 classifying four named traits from the evidence in front of you · Q7 the systematic nine-axis comparison · Q8 polygenic inheritance in the exact wording the schemes accept · Q9 the environment named and its mechanism given · Q10 genetically identical individuals that still differ · Q11 the whole Book in one answer. Q6 and Q7 are not the same question. Q7 wants the general table of axes with an explanation attached to each. Q6 wants you to read a specific stimulus and cite the specific evidence in it, which is where the examiner comment says candidates lose the marks. Q7 and Q11 are not the same essay either: Q7 is continuous against discontinuous, Q11 is how any combination of phenotypes arises at all.

Nothing from Books 7 to 9. Natural selection, evolution and the Hardy-Weinberg equation are Core Idea 4 and none of them is needed, even in the two essays. The phenotypic variance equation VP = VG + VE is not in the learning outcomes and does not appear. Neither do standard deviation, error bars, rates, dilution series or microscopy calibration, which belong to the Mathematical Requirements and Paper 4 rather than to LO 2(dd); the one piece of that material kept is reading a p value off published data, which the specimen asked for and which Q4(d) tests.
